business_scope.primary_industry_name: Mobile Utility Software and Device Performance Optimization Apps

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (mixed Napoleonic and Continental legal tradition; unitary national system with EU Treaty primacy)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and EU Common Commercial Policy
Agreement between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the People's Republic of China on the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (signed 1979)
Agreement between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the Kingdom of the Netherlands, Belgium, and Luxembourg (Benelux Economic Union) concerning economic and investment cooperation
Convention between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (signed 1996, as amended)
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between the European Union and Canada, as applicable through Luxembourg's EU membership

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (the 2004 AML/CFT Law); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 March 2019 implementing the RBE Law; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies, as amended; Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843, as transposed; Regulation (EU) No 2018/1672 on cash controls.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company house of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation (e.g., Companies House in the UK; Delaware Division of Corporations for US entities; EU commercial registers for EEA entities)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing state is a party to the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961; otherwise full consular legalization through the Luxembourg Embassy/Consulate in the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract of the corporate shareholder's board resolution authorising the incorporation of the Luxembourg SARL and designating signatures and representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or equivalent governing body of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification in the shareholder's jurisdiction followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of a valid passport or national identity card for each lawful beneficial owner, director, manager, and authorised signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport/ID issuing authority of the respective individual's country of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy by an approved public officer (notary or civil registry) in the individual's home jurisdiction; notarization plus Hague Apostille is strongly advised for non-EU individuals

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of physical residential address (utilities bill or recent bank statement) for each beneficial owner, director, and signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, municipal records, or a regulated bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified translation into French or German (where necessary) and, if requested, apostilled by the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter in relation to each shareholder and each beneficial owner, confirming the availability of funds and account conduct
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or consular legalization may be required if the bank is outside the EEA; originals in English, French, or German are preferred

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing a Luxembourg incorporation counsel or domiciliation agent, if applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent authority of the principal's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the country of grant and Hague Apostille; if the country is not an apostille party, consular legalization at the Luxembourg diplomatic mission

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, directors, and shareholders against the consolidated EU financial sanctions list, the UN Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN/Consolidated Sanctions list, and the national list published by the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance. PEP screening must cover politically exposed persons resident in domestic and foreign jurisdictions, their family members, and close associates, applying an enhanced due diligence standard consistent with the 2004 AML/CFT Law and Directives (EU) 2015/849 and (EU) 2018/843. Any match or unexplained risk flag requires a formal risk assessment, possible refusal of incorporation, and, if necessary, reporting to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU), the Cellule Renseignement Financier (CRF).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), accessible through the official e-portal MyGuichet.lu (https://www.lbr.lu / https://www.myguichet.lu) and the Luxembourg official publishing platform of the Mémorial / eLex system.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be expressed in Latin alphabetic characters. Luxembourg law does not mandate a specific national language for the corporate stem, but the legal form suffix must appear in French, German, or Luxembourgish as 'SARL', 'S.à r.l.', or 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée'. Names in non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic) must be transliterated into a Latin-alphabet rendering that is presented to the RCS; a certified transliteration/translation into French or German is required for use in the deed and the RCS filing. The name must be distinguishable from all prior trademarks and existing company names, must not be misleading, and must avoid any suggestion of purposes not contained in the articles of association.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event the RCS rejects a proposed name, the applicant or its Luxembourg notary may file a written administrative challenge with the Receveur du Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés within one month of the rejection notification. If the rejection is confirmed, the applicant may, within three months of the confirmation, file an appeal to the Tribunal administratif (Administrative Tribunal) of Luxembourg. A name reservation valid for 30 days may be extended by filing a fresh renewal request before expiry; if the reservation lapses, the name may be released. Upon any rejection, a new name clearance request with a distinct corporate stem may be filed immediately, and such a second filing does not require a further appeal fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited. A Luxembourg SARL must have a real registered office ('siège social') located in Luxembourg. A virtual office address may be acceptable for administrative correspondence only if the company also maintains physical premises or a contractual right to a physical meeting facility and a dedicated corporate address; the arrangement must satisfy the substance requirements set by the law of 19 December 2002 and by the circulars of the Luxembourg direct-tax authorities. A pure letterbox office, with no actual personnel or operational presence, is not permissible for an active mobile-utility app company. For the ISIC 6201 mobile app sector, a co-working or serviced-office location can comply, provided the company can establish local substance and management presence if audited.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 10–15% statistical probability within the first 12 months after incorporation for a low-risk digital-service company; the Luxembourg direct tax and social security administrations conduct substantive checks on newly registered SARLs, and an unannounced physical inspection is significantly more likely (estimated 25–35%) if the company has no employee, no lease, and no credible local management substance. EU and VAT compliance controls also raise the risk for cross-border digital app companies.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation (authentic act, statutes, and formalities before a Luxembourg notary)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary appointed by the parties and registered with the Luxembourg Chamber of Notaries
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial scale under the Law on notarial tariffs; market benchmark EUR 1,000–1,800 for a standard SARL incorporation deed.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS name clearance, registration of the company, and opening of the corporate folder (registre de commerce et des sociétés)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Administration de l'enregistrement et des domaines
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee schedule for the Law of 19 December 2002; approximate fee of EUR 85–110.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation notice in the Luxembourg official gazette (Mémorial C / eLex electronic publication)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Central Legislation Department of the Ministry of Justice / Luxembourg Business Registers publication system
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication fee as set by Grand-Ducal regulation; typical EUR 19–27.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of beneficial ownership information with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), managed under the Luxembourg Business Registers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory processing fee; EUR 15 if payable; no fee in certain electronic filing cases.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certificate of non-opposition and official extract of the commercial register (certificat de non-opposition and RCS extract)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory certificate fee schedule; approximately EUR 30–45 per document.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional legal due diligence, drafting of the articles of association, UBO analysis, and incorporation representation by a Luxembourg avocat
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm (Avocat à la Cour)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fixed fee for a standard SARL incorporation package: EUR 1,500–2,500, depending on corporate-shareholder complexity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of foreign corporate documents (estimated three sets of documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority of the foreign issuing state (Hague apostille authority) or Luxembourg diplomatic/consular mission where apostille is not available
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular and apostille tariffs set by the relevant foreign ministries; commonly EUR 30–50 per document.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation into French or German of non-Luxembourg corporate, banking, and identity documents, if required
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator registered with the Luxembourg Court of Appeal or an EU certified translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market per-word or per-page translation rate; EUR 50–100 per page for legal documents.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and domiciliation service for the first year (approved domiciliation agent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg professional domiciliation company (société de domiciliation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market annual fee for a low-risk SARL domiciliation: EUR 300–600 per year, including use of mailing address and legal correspondence.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales (Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies), as amended by the Law of 23 September 2020 on the Modernisation of Company Law, Articles 710-1 to 710-25 (governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée); Loi modifiée du 19 décembre 2002 sur le registre de commerce et des sociétés et la comptabilité des entreprises (RCS Law); Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 sur la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme (AML Law).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers S.A. (LBR), e-Justice electronic filing portal (www.rcs.lu).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial Deed of Incorporation (acte notarié de constitution) embedding the Articles of Association (statuts), filed electronically with the RCS by the Luxembourg notary, followed by publication of the registration extract in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Statutory minimum share capital is EUR 12,000, divided into shares of at least EUR 1 par value. At incorporation, at least 25% of each share must be paid up in cash (minimum EUR 3,000) and deposited into a blocked Luxembourg bank account in favor of the company; the remaining 75% must be fully paid within five years of incorporation. Contributions in kind require a valuation report by an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé). A single corporate or individual shareholder is permitted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED FIRST: That the Company be constituted as a private limited liability company (Société à Responsabilité Limitée) under the name and object stated in the Articles of Association, and that the subscribing partners accept the allotment of subscribed shares of EUR 1 par value each, representing the minimum capital of EUR 12,000. SECOND: That the registered office is fixed at 12, Rue de l'Innovation, L-1130 Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. THIRD: That [Name] is appointed as the first Manager (Gérant), with authority to manage, represent and bind the Company. FOURTH: That the Manager is instructed to deposit the subscribed capital, sign banking forms, and complete the notarization, RCS filing, RESA publication, UBO registration and tax registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Bank Account and Deposit of Minimum Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Luxembourg credit institution (e.g., BGL BNP Paribas, Spuerkeess, ING Luxembourg), central AML/KYC desk.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the future SARL or its subscribers. Provide corporate KYC documentation, identify underlying shareholders and beneficial owners, and wire-transfer the subscribed minimum capital (at least 25% of EUR 12,000, i.e., EUR 3,000) or the full EUR 12,000 if immediate full payment is chosen. Request a capital deposit certificate (attestation de blocage) stating the depositor, the amount, the account holder and the blocked-until-incorporation status. The certificate must be addressed to the Luxembourg notary and is generally valid for three to six months.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of all individual subscribers
Proof of residential address of each individual subscriber
Corporate KYC pack for any corporate partner (certificate of incorporation, register of shareholders, register of beneficial owners, audited or management financial statements)
Draft Articles of Association (statuts)
Bank account opening forms and AML questionnaire
Source of funds and source of wealth declaration
Business plan or activity description for AML risk assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the file, submit supplemental source-of-wealth evidence and an updated business plan; alternatively, open the account at a second Luxembourg bank or instruct the notary to hold the funds on escrow pending account approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Notarial Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary subject to the Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the notary to prepare the French-language deed of incorporation and the statuts, including corporate name, corporate object, registered office address, share capital, duration and management powers. The notary verifies the capital deposit certificate, performs AML identification under the 2004 AML Law, checks the availability of the corporate name against the RCS, and schedules the signing session. All subscribers or their duly authorized proxies sign the deed; the notary then authenticates the act, obtains the managers acceptance of office, and uploads the deed to the RCS electronic portal.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (statuts)
Valid capital deposit certificate (attestation de blocage)
Passport or identity card of all signatories
Duly executed notarial proxies, if applicable
RCS corporate name availability certificate or negative certificate
AML declarations and beneficial ownership statements
Written acceptance of office by the appointed Manager (Gérant)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects omissions or inconsistencies (e.g., defective object clause, insufficient capital certificate), amend and execute a rectification deed (acte rectificatif) or a fresh notarial deed; no earlier banking or filing steps are invalidated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing with the Register of Commerce and Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers, e-Justice online submission portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the signed notarial deed electronically with the RCS on the day of signing or the next business day and pays the statutory e-filing fee. The RCS verifies the legal form, corporate name, registered office, capital compliance and the Manager's powers, then allocates a single RCS identification number (numéro d'immatriculation) and issues the official RCS extract. The company acquires legal personality upon registration.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation (electronic certified copy)
RCS standard registration form (formulaire de dépôt)
Capital deposit certificate issued by the Luxembourg bank
Proof of registered office (lease agreement or notarized title)
Consent of the Manager to act (included in the deed)
Proof of payment of RCS filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or rectification request (e.g., name similarity, missing annex), the notary corrects the filing and resubmits within the applicable legal deadline; the file number is retained and no additional statutory fee is charged for the corrected filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Legal Notice in the Electronic Compendium
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Official Journal service (Journal officiel du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg) - Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS automatically transmits the registration extract for publication in RESA, which publishes the legal notice within five business days of registration. The publication renders the incorporation effective against third parties and completes the statutory publicity requirements.
required_dossiers: Automatic transmission by RCS (no separate application required)
RCS registration number and extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA notice is delayed, request an ex officio publication through the RCS helpdesk; if the published text contains errors, apply to the RCS for a corrected re-publication at no additional charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register of Beneficial Owners, Tax Registration and Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE - Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD) via MyGuichet.lu; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) if employees are hired.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: No later than one month after registration, file the beneficial owner declaration in the RBE register, disclosing all ultimate natural persons owning or controlling the SARL. Concurrently, register with the AEDT for VAT purposes and obtain the national identification number, and register with the ACD for corporate income tax and municipal business tax (impôt commercial). If the company staffs an office, register as an employer with the CCSS. Activate the MyGuichet/eCDF electronic mailbox and open the statutory corporate books (share register, minutes book, inventory book).
required_dossiers: RBE declaration form with names, nationalities, dates of birth, residency and ownership percentages of each beneficial owner
Certified copy of the Articles of Association and RCS extract
RCS registration certificate
Bank certificate evidencing payment of subscribed capital
VAT and corporate tax registration forms (formulaires 26 and 27 transmitted electronically)
Lease agreement of the registered office
Copy of the Manager's identity document
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE filing is rejected or late, file an amended declaration immediately and apply to the RCS for mitigation of late-filing fines; for tax registrations, correct the data through the MyGuichet rubrics and resubmit, with appeal available against any assessment or penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Chamber of Commerce Affiliation, Official Co-ordinates and Bank File Update
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chambre de Commerce du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg; optionally, Administration des contributions directes for electronic filing co-ordinates.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Every Luxembourg commercial company is legally affiliated to the Luxembourg Chamber of Commerce. Register the SARL in the Chamber's economic register and pay the annual affiliation contribution. Obtain the company's official Chamber of Commerce number, update the corporate bank account file with the final RCS extract and registration number, and finalize the statutory books by recording the allotment of shares and the appointment of the Manager.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
RBE registration receipt
Chamber of Commerce affiliation form
Certificate of registered office (lease agreement or title deed)
Bank account KYC update pack with RCS extract and Manager's identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber of Commerce returns the affiliation file, correct the UBO or address data and resubmit; settle any late affiliation contribution promptly with the Chamber to avoid collection enforcement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg (Ministère de l'Économie) - Directorate General for Industry, New Technologies and Research; no sectoral industrial manufacturing licence applies to pure software publishing activity under NACE 62.01 / ISIC 6201.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no operational or manufacturing permit is required for mobile utility software development and app-store distribution. The activity falls outside the list of licensed trades under the Law of 2 September 2011 on access to professions and does not trigger an establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement) because no physical retail or public-access premises are operated; distribution occurs exclusively through Apple App Store and Google Play Billing rails.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Agency of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Class 0/Exempt category: office-based software development is not listed in the annexes to the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment, and no EIA report, registration or environmental operating permit is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge or VOC emission points exist. The company must comply with municipal wastewater discharge ordinances for sanitary effluents from the registered office, the EU Waste Framework Directive 2008/98/EC for office waste sorting and recycling, the WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU for disposal of end-of-life IT hardware, and general Luxembourg waste-management regulations under the Law of 21 March 2012.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: obtain the fire-safety attestation (attestation de sécurité incendie) from the competent communal fire authority for the registered office under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 13 February 1989 on fire safety in buildings; standard leased office floors do not require structural load inspections as the landlord's building permit covers structural integrity. Occupational clearance: declare the workplace and employees, if any, with the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), implement first-aid equipment and emergency protocols under Articles L.311-15 and L.312-8 of the Luxembourg Labour Code, maintain electrical conformity statements for office equipment, and ensure workstation ergonomics compliance; a building permit (permis de construire) is required only if substantial interior alterations are made.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg has a split VAT/income tax administration: the Administration des contributions directes (ACD) is the competent authority for corporate income and municipal business tax, while the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) is the national VAT authority. Central filing and information portal: https://guichet.lu; direct tax portal: https://impotsdirects.public.lu; VAT portal: https://pfi.tax.lu (PFI electronic filing).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing an SARL must first complete notarial incorporation and register with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS), which issues a 13-digit national registration number. After RCS registration, the entity must apply for VAT identification with the AEDT using the standard registration form (Form 640), supplying the RCS excerpt, statutes, proof of registered office, identity of managers, and description of activities. For an SARL, no separate tax ID is needed for corporate income tax; the RCS number serves as the administrative identifier, while the AEDT issues a distinct VAT number in the format LU + 8 digits. Non-resident entities not establishing a permanent establishment must register directly with the AEDT for VAT from the first taxable transaction in Luxembourg, without a turnover threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not apply US-style check-the-box rules. A resident SARL is primarily taxable at entity level on worldwide income under the LIR. Available statutory elections include: (i) joint taxation of a resident parent and qualifying subsidiaries under Article 164bis LIR (tax consolidation) if the parent holds at least 95% of the subsidiary shares directly or indirectly; (ii) VAT grouping towards AEDT under Article 60 of the Luxembourg VAT law, allowing closely linked persons to be treated as a single taxable person; and (iii) the EU OSS (One-Stop-Shop) scheme election for intra-Community distance sales and cross-border B2C electronic services, subject to Luxembourg procedural requirements. Hybrid mismatch elections are restricted to the ATAD-aligned rules, and any elective structure must be commercially, legally, and economically substantive.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 (annual taxable turnover threshold for local small-business exemption for Luxembourg-established suppliers; no threshold for non-resident suppliers—registration is mandatory from the first taxable supply in Luxembourg; EU distance sales threshold of EUR 100,000 applies for EU suppliers unless OSS is used)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate a general real-time fiscal clearance system and has no API-based pre-clearance mandate for B2B invoices. B2G invoices to central government and public-sector bodies must be transmitted electronically in standardized formats (currently PEPPOL-compliant e-invoices). For B2B transactions, paper and PDF invoices remain valid provided they meet Luxembourg VAT invoice content requirements and are stored in a reliable, legible format. A mandatory domestic B2B e-invoicing regime has been announced with intended effect from 1 January 2026 (transitional period under discussion), but as of 2025 continuous transaction control, digital stamping, or mandatory reporting to the tax authority is not yet a legal requirement for private-sector invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for the supply of goods physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union by the seller or a third party acting on the seller's behalf, provided the future buyer is a non-EU person, the goods leave EU territory within the legally required time limits, and the supplier holds bona fide documentary evidence of export. For services, zero-rating applies under B2B place-of-supply rules where the customer is a taxable person established outside the EU, and for services directly connected to exported movable goods, provided the customer identification and service description are properly documented. For sales of the mobile utility app through Apple IAP or Google Play Billing to a non-EU consumer, the supply is an electronically supplied service taxed in the customer's residence country; to the extent the customer is EU-established, Luxembourg VAT at 17% applies (unless an OSS election covers the cross-border B2C supply), and the app store platform arrangements determine the operative tax treatment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (approved exit summary declaration showing the date and customs office of departure from the EU, retained in the company's VAT file)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (or equivalent transit document) evidencing physical dispatch of the goods outside EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer/payment settlement proof linking the foreign purchaser to the exported goods and demonstrating receipt of consideration in foreign currency or EUR
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT and customs authorities actively audit zero-export claims. Where the required proof of export is incomplete, absent, or inconsistent, the zero-rating is retrospectively denied and VAT at 17% is assessed on the initial supply value. The standard reassessment period is five years, extended to ten years in cases of fraud, falsification of documents, or deliberate concealment. Delinquent VAT charges attract late-payment interest at the statutory monthly rate of 0.8%, and administrative penalties can reach EUR 25,000; participation in a VAT carousel or knowing submission of false export declarations exposes the company and its managers to criminal tax-fraud sanctions, civil fines, imprisonment in severe cases, and EU-wide cross-border information-sharing through the Eurofisc network.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the European System of Central Banks (ESCB); the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) supervises credit institutions and payment/electronic-money institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility for the euro. Capital movements are fully liberalized under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU); no exchange-control licensing applies to equity injections, shareholder loans, trade settlements, or profit remittances. Profit remittance is subject only to standard corporate tax formalities: no withholding tax on dividends paid to qualifying EU/EEA corporate shareholders under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive 2011/96/EU, otherwise 15% domestic dividend withholding, reducible under Luxembourg's extensive tax treaty network. No convertibility restrictions, foreign-investment approvals, or documentary FX clearances are imposed by the BCL.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory repatriation timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation for export proceeds. EUR invoicing is the default; USD and other-currency receipts from Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, or direct B2B licenses may be retained in foreign-currency accounts or converted freely. The only relevant requirement is the BCL statistical balance-of-payments (BoP) reporting obligation triggered when an individual cross-border transaction or aggregate monthly flows exceed the applicable de minimis threshold (typically EUR 12,500), with no punitive or administrative consent requirement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility as an ancillary collection and payout vehicle; Medium as a primary treasury bank. A CSSF-licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI) under the Luxembourg law of 21 December 2007 (as amended) and PSD2 may lawfully issue e-money wallets, execute payment transactions, hold safeguarding accounts, and provide FX conversion. However, EMIs cannot grant credit or lending facilities, and safeguarding requirements restrict idle client funds. For this SARL's digitally sourced revenue (Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, subscription), the optimal configuration is a hybrid treasury: a regulated Luxembourg bank as the operating/escrow account for capital injections, payroll, supplier disbursements, and a CSSF-regulated EMI or Payment Institution (PI) as an optional collection/settlement account for distributing storefront payout proceeds. Use of an offshore (non-EU) EMI is discouraged due to CSSF supervision gaps and corresponding correspondent-bank de-risking risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No mandatory physical attendance in Luxembourg. Remote onboarding is permissible under the CSSF KYC framework (notably CSSF Circulars 19/716 and 20/744) via video-identification performed by an authorized professional (regulated bank, notary, or CSSF-recognized video-verification provider) with liveness detection and NFC-capable document validation. Beneficial owners must be filed in the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE); foreign directors/UBOs may execute account-opening documentation remotely via apostilled powers of attorney. A recorded remote KYC interview is standard practice, but in-person visits may be waived for a low-risk software SARL whose shareholders and directors are identified in the notarial deed of incorporation and the RBE excerpt. Required dossier: notarial deed of incorporation and statuts, RCS extract, RBE excerpt, board resolution appointing account signatories, proof of registered office, source-of-funds/wealth evidence, and specimen signatures. Banks typically require a signed account agreement returned by post/courier from the registered office to finalize opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or director tax residence in a jurisdiction without full KYC reciprocity, or opaque intermediary holding structures above the SARL.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Equity structure chart with exact ownership percentages; notarized/certified copies of all intermediate entities' constitutive documents; certificate of incumbency from licensed corporate agents; UBO passports and recent proof of address; notarized source-of-wealth declaration for all funding shareholders; audited financial statements of the direct parent if available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO flagged in sanctions/PEP databases or jurisdictional overlap with high-risk territories.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative screening results from a recognized compliance data provider (e.g., Dow Jones, Refinitiv, World-Check); signed PEP-status declaration; for any PEP exposure, an independent validation that funds do not derive from public office, complemented by a legal opinion from a Luxembourg counsel confirming the corporate purpose and absence of sanctions nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared freemium mobile utility model and projected payment volumes, especially high-frequency, low-value storefront chargebacks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan with revenue model and financial projections; Apple Developer / Google Play payout statements and chargeback-rate report; platform agreements with Apple and Google; anti-fraud policy and app-content compliance documentation; reconciliation workflow audit trail linking IAP/Play billing to monthly settlement statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident management with minimal physical Luxembourg substance or family-governance structure without local nexus.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Employment contracts of local resident staff; registered-office lease agreement; minutes of board meetings physically held in Luxembourg; engagement letter with a Luxembourg corporate-services/fiduciary firm; payroll and social-security filings; filing confirmation of annual accounts with the RCS; VAT registration certificate with the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital increase: execution of a notarial deed before a Luxembourg notary, followed by registration with the RCS and publication formalities; funds remitted via SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR) with remittance information referencing the notarial deed date and purpose, e.g., 'Capital increase per notarial deed dd.mm.yyyy – subscribed shares'; the bank issues the statutory certificate of subscription deposit (attestation légale de souscription et de libération) required for the RCS filing. Shareholder loan: written loan agreement with arm's-length interest rate aligned with transfer-pricing guidance (AEA/CV-CI 5.0); wire reference 'Shareholder loan agreement dd.mm.yyyy'; three months of source-of-funds bank statements from the lending shareholder. No BCL authorization or foreign-investment approval is required; only the BCL BoP statistical threshold (approx. EUR 12,500) triggers reporting. All inbound EUR wires should use purpose code 'LOAN' or 'EQUITY' as applicable and must be reconcilable to the signed corporate documentation to avoid AML holds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail for EUR payables is SEPA Credit Transfer (SEPA CT) with TARGET2 for high-value same-day settlements. For non-EUR trade settlements (USD, GBP, CHF), use SWIFT MT103 serial or cover payment routed via the Luxembourg bank's correspondent network (typically New York/London branches); remittance fields must include invoice number, contract reference, and buyer code to prevent false-positive AML screening. Trade settlement for significant supplier contracts may be effected via irrevocable letter of credit (SWIFT MT700) or documentary collection (SWIFT MT400/MT4xx). Inbound Apple IAP/Google Play Billing proceeds arrive via the operators' payout systems as scheduled ACH/SEPA or wire credits into the pre-registered treasury account; reconciliation must map the operator settlement statements to the app-store service period. For intercompany flows to group entities, use SEPA CT or MT103 with financial-purpose codes (e.g., 'INTRA' or 'FIN') and demonstrate transfer-pricing compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD forwards and outright currency forwards under standard ISDA/CSA master agreements with the relationship bank, with maturity aligned to the Apple/Google payout cycles
FX swaps (EUR/USD spot-forward combination) for efficient rolling treasury liquidity management
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) to hedge medium-term shareholder loans or long-term intercompany capital exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) — legally permissible but limited to restricted-currency exposures; not recommended for EUR/USD because of the euro's full convertibility and actively deliverable market
Amortizing FX forwards structured to match the expected monthly remittances from US app-store revenue, reducing residual open exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) with directors' report, auditor's report (if any) and list of shareholders; electronic deposit with the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) eJustice portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM approval within 6 months of year-end (calendar year: by 30 June); RCS deposit within 1 month of approval (calendar year: by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Graduated administrative fines up to EUR 1,500 for late deposit; court referral and possible judicial strike-off/dissolution for persistent default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) – annual confirmation and change updates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RBE register (Ministry of Justice)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Update within 1 month of any change in shareholding; annual confirmation at least once per calendar year (anniversary-based reminder from LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines EUR 250–250,000; conviction publicity; responsible officers personally liable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax and municipal business tax return (AI + IMC) via eCDF
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 December of the year following the tax year (calendar-year FY 2025 return due 31 December 2026); 6-month extension available on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest 0.6% per month; late-filing penalty up to 10% of assessed tax; enforced collection

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net wealth tax return (impôt sur la fortune – IFT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 December of the tax year (calendar-year FY 2025 return due 31 December 2025); filed simultaneously with CIT return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest 0.6% per month; minimum IFT (EUR 535 or EUR 1,000) applies regardless of losses; enforced collection

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a réviseur d'entreprises (agréé) where the SARL exceeds two of three thresholds at balance-sheet date: balance-sheet total EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average 50 employees; audit is also compulsory where shares are held by more than 25 persons or the articles of association so provide (Art. 70-1, Law of 10 August 1915)
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2008 on annual accounts, transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU); EU-endorsed IFRS permitted for non-listed companies and mandatory for listed groups

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Any SARL share transfer requires a notarial deed (Luxembourg notary) and RCS registration; the RBE declaration must be updated within 1 month of the resulting change in beneficial ownership and the full RBE dataset must be confirmed at least annually via the LBR portal; upon UBO changes an updated list of shareholders is filed with the RCS together with the notarial deed
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute book (Registre des procès-verbaux des assemblées)
Register of Beneficial Owners (internal RBE records and supporting documentation)
Accounting books and supporting documents (Art. 17, Luxembourg Code de commerce)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Aggregate headline rate in Luxembourg City is approximately 24.94%: 17% corporate income tax (CIT) plus 7% solidarity surcharge, plus 6.75% municipal business tax. Qualifying mobile-app software IP income benefits from the Luxembourg IP regime, which grants an 80% exemption on net eligible IP income, reducing the effective CIT on that IP income to approximately 5.2%. Dividends and capital gains derived from qualifying shareholdings of 10% or more, held for at least 12 months, may be 100% exempt under the participation exemption. A preferential investment tax credit for digitalisation expenditures is available; no general statutory tax holiday applies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite for losses incurred from 1 January 2017; a 10-year limitation continues to apply to losses incurred before 2017

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Luxembourg Corporate Tax Return Form 451 (Formulaire 451 – Déclaration de l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités et de l'impôt commercial communal), filed electronically on the Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) professional e-space via guichet.public.lu / MyGuichet with Luxtrust or eIDAS authentication.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly prepayments of estimated CIT and municipal business tax are separately due for companies assessed above ACD de-minimis thresholds.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year SARL, Form 451 must be filed by 31 May of the following year. For a non-calendar financial year, the return must be filed within five months after the balance-sheet date. An electronic extension request may move the filing deadline to 31 July; further extension is discretionary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 451, Section 1 – Identification and shareholder register
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, RCS Luxembourg number, national tax matricule number, registered office, date of incorporation, balance-sheet date, and the identity and percentage ownership of each shareholder and director.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the country of tax residence of every non-resident shareholder and director. No foreign tax identification number must be entered on the Luxembourg form unless the ACD specifically requests it; attach a share register for dividend WHT assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 451, Section 5 – Gross revenue by sales channel
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross receipts from mobile utility app sales, in-app purchases, subscriptions, advertising, and any B2B licensing, disaggregated by Apple App Store, Google Play, and direct enterprise channels. App-store commissions are disclosed as deductible distribution costs, not as IP royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report revenue on the Luxembourg entity’s invoicing and accounting basis; if books are kept in USD rather than EUR, attach a consistent foreign-exchange schedule and disclose conversion methodology to the ACD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back non-deductible expenses, including fines, excessive entertainment, non-arm's-length intercompany charges, and the disallowed portion of net interest expense under ATAD. Deduct payroll, office rent, depreciation, server hosting, and arm's-length intercompany service fees substantiated by a transfer-pricing study.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If management or technical fees are payable to non-resident related shareholders, attach service descriptions, evidence of actual performance, and an OECD-compliant arm's-length benchmark; otherwise the deduction is denied and the payment may be reclassified as a constructive dividend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List dividend income and capital gains from qualifying EU or non-EU participations of at least 10%, or where the acquisition cost is at least EUR 1.2 million, and the shares have been held for at least 12 months. Claim the 100% exemption where the characterisation requirements are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident shareholder receiving dividend flows through the SARL, attach the subsidiary’s legal form and tax-residence certificate to support the participation exemption; passive portfolio losses are not shelterable through this section.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute net income derived from qualifying mobile-app software, related copyrights, and patented features; apply the 80% exemption on eligible net IP income and reconcile the result with IP registration documentation, development cost records, and the ACD IP regime filing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The economic ownership, development, and decision-making functions for the IP must be located in Luxembourg. If the app IP was acquired from a non-resident related party at an artificially low or high price, the IP regime is denied and a transfer-pricing adjustment will be imposed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 451, Section 10 – Municipal business tax and net wealth tax basis
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the taxable basis for municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) and for net wealth tax. Include the mobile-app intangible asset at its accounting carrying value except where the IP regime or participation exemption excludes it.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Luxembourg-resident SARL is subject to net wealth tax on worldwide assets unless a tax treaty protects specific assets; non-resident owners must ensure that the SARL’s bank accounts and app receivables are disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 451, Section 12 – CIT and municipal business tax computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 17% CIT rate to the final taxable base, add the 7% solidarity surcharge, and apply the municipal business tax rate of the relevant commune. Deduct previously paid quarterly instalments and any foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident shareholders, no dividend distribution should be recorded in the tax computation unless the general meeting has declared it; undistributed reserves remain within the SARL and do not attract dividend WHT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file by the statutory deadline exposes the SARL to an ex-officio assessment (taxation d'office) based on estimated assets. The ACD can issue a formal filing summons (sommation) with an additional surcharge of up to EUR 250 and a general late-filing penalty of up to EUR 10,000 under the Luxembourg General Tax Act. Unpaid tax accrues delay interest at 0.6% per month. In cases of fraudulent concealment, the responsible officer may be subject to a criminal surcharge of up to 10% of the evaded tax and imprisonment risk.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain a reduced dividend withholding rate or an exemption at source, the beneficial owner must deliver a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by its country of tax residence before the dividend payment. The Luxembourg paying agent must file Form 251 (application for reduced withholding tax) with the ACD or otherwise withhold at the statutory 15%. For an EU/EEA parent, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive may exempt withholding entirely if the parent holds at least 10% of the SARL’s capital or voting rights for an uninterrupted 12-month period and the arrangement is not abusive. Over-withheld tax may be recovered through a Luxembourg refund procedure; adequate economic substance in the SARL is essential to prevent denial of treaty or directive benefits under the anti-abuse doctrine.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no statutory withholding tax on outbound royalties or interest paid to non-resident beneficial owners; treaty rates are also effectively 0%. However, excessive, artificial, or non-arm's-length interest and royalty flows can be recharacterised as constructive dividends subject to the 15% dividend WHT, and the deduction may be denied under ATAD interest limitation rules and general anti-abuse principles.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No de-minimis statutory threshold is codified in the LIR. In practice, the Luxembourg tax authorities expect an OECD-compliant Master File and Local File when the MNE group has consolidated revenue of at least EUR 50 million; for a Luxembourg SARL with cross-border related-party transactions exceeding EUR 500,000 per fiscal year, a Local File and benchmarking study should be maintained. Country-by-Country notification applies where the ultimate parent group has consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies an overriding economic-substance doctrine grounded in the statutory general anti-abuse rule (Abuse of Laws) and OECD BEPS principles. A SARL distributing mobile-app revenue must demonstrate real local presence, payroll, office space, local board decision-making, bank accounts, and substantive control over the software IP. If the SARL is a shell with assets and risks formally owned but functionally controlled from abroad, the ACD may disregard the entity, deny treaty benefits, disallow IP-box relief, and reassess income at the full Luxembourg CIT, solidarity surcharge, and municipal business tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Wilful tax evasion and fraudulent misdeclaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly under-reporting Apple App Store and Google Play Billing gross revenue, inflating deductible app-store commissions, or creating fictitious backdated service invoices to reduce Luxembourg taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud proceedings may lead to imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to EUR 250,000, in addition to restitution of all underpaid CIT, solidarity surcharge, municipal business tax, and late interest at 0.6% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing fraudulent returns are jointly and severally liable for the evaded corporate taxes and may be disqualified from managing Luxembourg companies for up to 10 years; travel bans and attachment of personal assets may be ordered during penal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and absence of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SARL with no employees, no Luxembourg office, no local bank account, no minutes of actual board decisions, and holding the mobile-app IP solely for treaty shopping while all functions are performed by a non-resident parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD may apply the anti-abuse doctrine and disregard the SARL as a fiscally transparent vehicle; income is reassessed at the Luxembourg resident shareholder level, treaty benefits are denied, and all previously exempt IP-box income becomes taxable at the aggregate 24.94% rate plus penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be summoned personally to restore distributions made without substance, may be held liable for unpaid withholding taxes, and, in egregious cases, face criminal prosecution for abusive use of a legal entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing manipulation and hidden royalty leakage
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying non-arm's-length royalties, management fees, or licence costs to a related entity in a zero-tax jurisdiction without a TP study, or adopting a margin that leaves the Luxembourg SARL with no residual profit from the mobile-app business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 56 LIR, the ACD may make a transfer-pricing adjustment increasing the taxable base, deny the deduction of the excessive payment, and impose a late-payment surcharge plus delay interest; absence of contemporaneous documentation attracts additional penalties and a 10% surcharge on the adjustment in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly implemented an artificial pricing scheme are personally liable for the company’s tax shortfall to the extent of their benefit, can be barred from board memberships, and may be subject to extradition proceedings if they leave Luxembourg while a tax criminal inquiry is active.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML non-compliance and misdirected payment flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing App Store / Google Play proceeds through undisclosed offshore bank accounts, using non-registered payment service providers, or layering app revenue through shell invoices to obscure beneficial ownership and evade Luxembourg tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg AML framework, money laundering is punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to EUR 5 million; aggravated tax fraud may raise the penalty to 7 years’ imprisonment. The ACD and Financial Intelligence Unit may also freeze corporate and personal accounts and seize the mobile-app revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors found to have participated knowingly in the laundering structure face personal criminal conviction, travel bans, professional disqualification, and civil restitution of all laundered funds, with no statutory cap on damages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to file, obstructing the tax audit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Ignoring ACD requests for Form 451, refusing to submit accounting records, bank statements, share registers, server cost records, or transfer-pricing documentation, and preventing a field audit of the Luxembourg SARL.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD can issue an estimated taxation d'office on a high deemed basis, with a formal penalty of up to EUR 10,000 for non-filing and additional monthly delay interest. Obstructing an audit is a separate administrative offence that may be escalated to a criminal fine of up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment if obstruction is intentional.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who fail to cooperate are personally liable for penalties, may have their passports suspended while an obstructed tax audit is pending, and can be prosecuted for fraud if the obstruction conceals taxable app revenue.
